items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> at the left edge, and beside it the entire shape of a <radical>run</radical> — thigh forward, foot planting, ground coming loose behind. Except there is no horse here, no cart, and no road worth the name. Whatever is getting done today is getting done <radical>on foot</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle has never once taken a ride. He carries the sample doors on his shell and walks the entire round, and he announces himself at every house with the same syllable before he knocks — 「<reading>と</reading>」. と, and another mile.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Your own <radical>self</radical> sits on top — that nose you point at when you mean you — and directly underneath it, your <radical>heart</radical>. Nose above, heart below, and running between the two of them all day long is the one thing you never have to decide to do. In through the nose, down to the heart, back out: <radical>breath</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Soku is the swimmer who comes up after far too long under and takes one enormous ragged gulp — 「<reading>そく</reading>」 — nose first, heart going like a hammer. That is what a breath you badly needed sounds like. そく.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Three strokes and nothing else: a curve like the shoulder of a hill, with one line falling through it. It is the moon, only half up and not yet bright, caught at the exact moment the light goes flat and blue and everything loses its edges. Nothing has happened yet. The whole character is one picture of <radical>evening</radical> starting.
items.reading_mnemonic: Seki comes out onto his step at this hour every night, and you hear him before you see him — that wet, rattling 「<reading>せき</reading>」 of a cough carrying right down the street. When せき starts up, the light has gone.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone has swept the whole yard with a <radical>broom</radical>, one stroke that <radical>slides</radical> away to the left, until the <radical>ground</radical> is spotless. Then he opens his <radical>mouth</radical> and gives out tomorrow's orders. He is not the emperor, only the man directly above you — the <radical>mister</radical> whose name gets attached to every younger man in the room.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kun is the teacher who refuses to use first names. Every boy in the class gets the same syllable barked after his surname — 「<reading>くん</reading>」 — as the seating chart comes out. Tanaka-くん. Sato-くん. It is how you know he means you.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> on the left, and beside it the <radical>small</radical> mark. Not the ear, not the stalk — one single bristle off the very top of the head, the thinnest thing on the entire plant. Slice up an hour the same way and the sliver you are left holding is one <radical>second</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Byou is the hospital timekeeper with the stopwatch, and she counts out loud in a flat clipped bark — 「<reading>びょう</reading>」, びょう, びょう — one for every tick. She will not speed up and she will not stop. びょう is a single second landing.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>wide box</radical> of a room, and shoved right to the back of it a store of <radical>rice</radical> with something <radical>big</radical> planted on top of the pile. You have to walk through every other room in the house to reach it, and nobody outside the family ever does. The deepest room is the building's <radical>heart</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ou is the grandmother who lives in that back room and has not come out in years. Knock and you get one long syllable through the paper door — 「<reading>おう</reading>」 — meaning she heard you and no, you may not come in. おう, from the very back of the house.
